claims.claim: In 2026 there were just over 250,000 visits to B.C. food banks, up 100 per cent since 2019 and 14 per cent from 2025, with nearly 76,000 visits from children.
claims.episode_span: monthly visits to B.C. food banks at just over 250,000 in 2026, up 100 per cent since 2019 and 14 per cent from 2025
claims.source_title: B.C. food bank use has increased by a shocking amount since 2019
claims.supporting_quote: In 2026, there were just over 250,000 visits to B.C. food banks, with nearly 76,000 of those being from children.

claims.claim: Kirstin Beardsley said people are choosing between food and rent and that the days of absorbing a small setback are over.
claims.episode_span: those days are over, with people choosing between food and rent
claims.source_title: B.C. food bank use has increased by a shocking amount since 2019
claims.supporting_quote: Canada’s bleak new reality is that millions of people are making impossible trade-offs every day as they choose between food or rent,” said Kirstin Beardsley, Food Banks Canada CEO, in a statement.

claims.claim: Food Banks Canada reported 18 per cent of clients are employed and that people with the lowest incomes spend about 60 per cent of disposable income on housing.
claims.episode_span: 18 per cent of clients are employed, that people with the lowest incomes spend about 60 per cent of disposable income on housing
claims.source_title: B.C. food bank use has increased by a shocking amount since 2019
claims.supporting_quote: Further, Food Banks Canada reported that 18 per cent of food bank clients are employed. It found that people with the lowest incomes spend about 60 per cent of their disposable income on housing.

claims.claim: Innovative Research Group's October 15-19 poll of 1,153 people found 43 per cent of decided voters for the B.C. Conservatives, 38 per cent for the NDP and 12 per cent for the Greens.
claims.episode_span: 43 per cent of decided voters backing the B.C. Conservatives, 38 per cent the B.C. NDP and 12 per cent the B.C. Greens
claims.source_title: B.C. Election: Big jump in voters wanting change is the 'kiss of death' for NDP leader David Eby, says pollster
claims.supporting_quote: On Tuesday, Innovative Research Group president Greg Lyle said the poll showed 43 per cent of decided voters were backing the B.C. Conservatives, compared to 38 per cent for the B.C. NDP. The B.C. Green party have 12 per cent of decided voters.

claims.claim: Greg Lyle said the share of voters who think it is time for a change rose eight points to 65 per cent since the election was called.
claims.episode_span: the share who think it is time for a change rose eight points, to 65 per cent
claims.source_title: B.C. Election: Big jump in voters wanting change is the 'kiss of death' for NDP leader David Eby, says pollster
claims.supporting_quote: Lyle noted that his poll found that there had been an eight per cent increase in the number of voters who think it’s time for a change in government, to 65 per cent, compared to when Eby called the election just under a month ago.

claims.claim: Vancouver mayor-elect Pete Fry endorsed B.C. Green leader Emily Lowan on Vancouver Island on Tuesday.
claims.episode_span: Pete Fry travelled to Vancouver Island to endorse B.C. Green candidate and leader Emily Lowan
claims.source_title: B.C. Election: Big jump in voters wanting change is the 'kiss of death' for NDP leader David Eby, says pollster
claims.supporting_quote: Meanwhile, on Tuesday Vancouver mayor-elect Pete Fry travelled to Vancouver Island to endorse B.C. Green party candidate and leader Emily Lowan.

claims.claim: The B.C. government agreed to pay $35 million to settle a class action on behalf of more than 100 prisoners who alleged sexual assault by a jail guard in their youth.
claims.episode_span: pay $35 million to settle a class-action lawsuit on behalf of more than 100 prisoners
claims.source_title: B.C. pays $35 million to settle lawsuit by prisoners sexually assaulted by guard
claims.supporting_quote: The B.C. government has agreed to pay $35 million to settle a class-action lawsuit on behalf of more than 100 prisoners who alleged they were sexually assaulted in their youth by a B.C. jail guard.

claims.claim: Doug McCallum said only the B.C. Conservatives have committed to SkyTrain to Newton, while the B.C. NDP offered a meeting.
claims.episode_span: only the B.C. Conservatives have committed to expanding SkyTrain to Newton, while the B.C. NDP offered a meeting
claims.source_title: BC NDP, BC Conservatives support expanding SkyTrain to Newton
claims.supporting_quote: The city's newly elected mayor, Doug McCallum, said in a statement that only the BC Conservatives have committed to the expansion, while the BC NDP "offered a meeting."

claims.claim: Hudson's Hope voters approved borrowing up to $10 million for a community hall whose construction is estimated at more than $34 million.
claims.episode_span: approved borrowing up to $10 million to help finance a new community hall
claims.source_title: Hudson's Hope voters approve borrowing for new community hall, construction estimated to cost more than $34M
claims.supporting_quote: Residents in Hudson's Hope, B.C., have approved borrowing up to $10 million dollars to help finance a new community hall and multi-use gathering space, decided through referendum voting on Saturday.

claims.source_title: Stalled Downtown Vancouver office tower project pivots to 295-room hotel
claims.supporting_quote: It now calls for a 362 ft. tall (110.5 metres) tower with 32 storeys, containing almost 158,000 sq. ft. of total building floor area.

claims.claim: The Hurricanes beat the Canucks 6-3 at Rogers Arena, with Deslauriers, Ehlers and Stankoven each scoring twice, and the Canucks have lost eight in a row.
claims.episode_span: The Carolina Hurricanes beat the Vancouver Canucks 6-3 on Tuesday at Rogers Arena.
claims.source_title: Hurricanes score six, pull away from slumping Canucks
claims.supporting_quote: Nicolas Deslauriers , Nikolaj Ehlers and Logan Stankoven each scored their second goal of the game in the third period for the Carolina Hurricanes in a 6-3 win against the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Arena on Tuesday.

claims.claim: David Eby promised $30 million to finish the unused sixth floor at Kelowna General Hospital, and Gavin Dew said a Conservative government would open the unused space after reviewing Interior Health capital planning.
claims.episode_span: promising $30 million to finish the unused sixth floor at Kelowna General Hospital
claims.source_title: Eby’s $30M hospital expansion pledge draws questions over timing
claims.supporting_quote: With the provincial election just days away, BC NDP Leader David Eby is promising $30 million to finish the unused sixth floor at Kelowna General Hospital.
